high.title: Selic Drops to 14%, but Petrobras (PETR4) Moves Markets; Ibovespa in Dollars Rises Today (Aug 6)
high.summary: The Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) delivered a 25 basis point cut to the Selic rate, bringing it from 14.25% to 14.00% per annum — a move that was fully priced in by the market. The key takeaway was the tone of the accompanying COPOM statement: the central bank adopted a notably cautious posture and deliberately avoided forward guidance on the pace or magnitude of future rate cuts. Despite this hawkish communication, economists interpreted the statement constructively, noting that the BCB acknowledged a gradual deceleration in economic activity alongside a marginal improvement in current inflation readings.

high.title: Petrobras (PETR4): ADRs Advance in New York on Above-Expectation Earnings and Dividends
high.summary: Petrobras reported Q2 2026 net income of R$52.4 billion, surpassing market consensus expectations. The results are being positively received in pre-market trading in New York, with ADRs tied to ordinary shares (PBR) rising 0.76% to US$18.66, while preferred share ADRs (PBRa) advanced 1.52% to US$16.73 as of 7:20am BRT. The strong earnings were driven by record oil and gas production, higher commodity prices, and improved refining margins. Dividend announcements are also back in focus for investors.

high.title: Market Reacts to Petrobras' Billion-Dollar Dividend; Ibovespa in Dollar Terms Falls Today (7)
high.summary:
Markets are digesting Petrobras' (PETR3; PETR4) Q2 2026 results released Thursday, alongside a significant dividend announcement. The state-controlled oil giant posted net income of R$52.4 billion for the quarter, beating market consensus of R$50.8 billion. Management attributed the outperformance to record oil and derivatives production, elevated Brent crude prices, and strong cash generation. Despite the earnings beat, the Ibovespa is declining in USD terms on the day, suggesting BRL weakness is offsetting any equity gains in dollar-adjusted terms — a key metric for international fund managers benchmarking in USD. The billion-dollar dividend announcement is notable as it implies significant capital repatriation flows, which could have near-term implications for BRL liquidity and foreign investor positioning. Petrobras remains the single largest weight on the Ibovespa, meaning its price action will dominate index performance. Watch for any government commentary on dividend policy, as political interference risk around Petrobras payouts remains a perennial concern for foreign equity and FX investors alike.

medium.title: Petrobras (PETR4): What to Expect from the Earnings Report? Dividends Back in Focus
medium.summary:
Published ahead of Petrobras' Q2 2026 results release (after market close on August 6), this preview highlighted analyst consensus projecting net revenue of approximately R$30.8 billion, with stronger sequential performance driven by record oil and gas output, elevated commodity prices, and improved refining margins. Dividends were flagged as the key focus point for investors going into the print. The article set the stage for what proved to be an above-consensus result. For equity and macro investors, Petrobras dividend flows carry fiscal relevance as the Brazilian federal government, as controlling shareholder, receives a significant share — directly impacting primary fiscal balance projections. Watch for the official dividend announcement and payout timeline as a near-term catalyst.
